issues.description: Directory-only zip entries are created in Unzip.initExtractFile's isDirectory() mkdirs branch and never pass through UnzipEngine.unzipFile, so a malicious directory entry (e.g. '../../evil/') can still create directories outside the target dir; the official fix guards this branch, ours does not.
Patch commits generated build artifacts (target/maven-status *.lst files, pom.properties) unrelated to the fix, reducing cleanliness of the diff.

pov_before_reproduced=false and regressions_ran=0 mean the harness did not positively demonstrate the pre-patch trigger or run regression tests, so functional/behavioral confirmation is weaker than ideal.

result.summary: Our patch applies the correct CWE-022 defense-of-record — canonicalize the resolved output file and verify it stays within the canonical output directory using a proper separator boundary — placed directly at the file-write sink in UnzipEngine.unzipFile, which is arguably a better location than the official fix and avoids the prefix-match weakness in the official startsWith check. It closes the primary zip-slip file-write attack class. However, it does not cover the directory-only extraction branch (Unzip.initExtractFile's mkdirs) that the official fix guards, leaving directory-entry traversal unaddressed, and the diff includes unrelated build artifacts.
result.root_cause: Untrusted zip entry names flow into new File(outPath + name) and are written without verifying the resolved absolute path stays inside the intended extraction directory, allowing writes outside the target dir (zip slip).
